units.tr: Conclusio. Manlius should therefore be acquitted, if not by strict right, at least by the grace of the Emperor, his father. And all the more so because this battle was salutary, and as it were approved by God himself through the joyful victory.

units.la: Decretum fuit, ut percutiatur securi.
units.tr: It was decreed that he be struck with the axe.

units.la: THEMA XVI.
units.tr: THEME XVI.

units.la: Accusatio Mommorancii Domini Bouteville ob commissum Parisiis in foro Regio duellum, contra Edictum Regium.
units.tr: Accusation of the Marquis de Bouteville for the duel fought in the public square at Paris, contrary to the royal Edict.

units.la: Exord. Causæ pondus exponit à comparatione delicti & personæ delinquentis.
units.tr: Exordium. He sets out the weight of the case by comparing the offence with the person who committed it.

units.la: I. Delictum tale est, quod nobilitati familiare, legibus omnibus & Edicto Regio contrarium, Galliæ imprimis funestum; ubi plus generosi sanguinis per duella, quàm per bella effunditur.
units.tr: I. Such an offence is common among the nobility, contrary to all laws and to the royal Edict, and above all deadly to France, where more noble blood is spilled in duels than in wars.

units.la: II. Persona ex antiquissima Principum Galliæ familia cum plurimis duellis famigerata; inter quæ ultimum, quod nuperrimè à Domino Butevillio contra Malchionem de Bevron & Buffio patratum.
units.tr: II. The person comes from the most ancient family of the princes of France and is notorious for many duels, the latest of which was recently carried out by the Lord de Bouteville against Malchion de Bevron and Buffy.

units.la: Propos. Hac propter reum ipsum hic sisti, & ex lege ad ultimum supplicium posci ex mandato regis, qui causam Parlamento extra ordinem commiserit.
units.tr: Proposition. For this reason the accused is to be brought before this court and, by law, sentenced to the extreme penalty, by command of the king, who has committed the case to Parliament outside the ordinary course.

units.la: Confirmatio.
units.tr: Confirmation.

units.la: I. Ex ratione facti, utpote quod
units.tr: I. From the nature of the deed, namely that

units.la: a. Profectum sit ex animo obstinato adversus leges. Quia Butevillius ob duella crebra exul, ausus sit venire Parisios, provocare ad duellum in loco publico; Exaggerentur singulæ circumstantiæ.
units.tr: a. It was done from a stubborn spirit against the laws. Bouteville, an exile for his frequent duels, dared to come to Paris and challenge a man to a duel in a public place. Each circumstance is to be stressed.

units.la: b. Perpetratum contra personam innoxiam, quam ex vana ambitione Parisios sectatus sit.
units.tr: b. It was committed against an innocent person, whom he pursued to Paris out of vain ambition.

units.la: c. Vergat in pessimam consequentiam, videl. conculcationem Edicti regii & regiæ autoritatis.
units.tr: c. It tends to the worst consequence, namely the trampling underfoot of the royal Edict and of royal authority.

units.la: II. Ex testimoniis, videl.
units.tr: II. From the testimonies, namely:

units.la: a. Legibus naturalibus, divinis & humanis, quibus prohibitum homicidium & proinde duella : quippe in quibus est 1. Violatio justitiæ; sæpe enim cadit lælus & innocens 2. Usurpatio juris majestatis, utpote ad quam pertinet jus gladii.
units.tr: a. The natural, divine and human laws, by which homicide is forbidden, and therefore duels: for in them there is (1) a violation of justice, since the joyful and innocent often fall; (2) a usurpation of the right of majesty, since the right of the sword belongs to it.

units.la: b. Edicto regio contra duella, repetito toties in Gallia, ubi capitale statuitur duellum.
units.tr: b. The royal Edict against duels, repeated so often in France, where a duel is punishable by death.

units.la: c. Judicato in persona ipsius Butevillii, qui jampridem ob duella proscriptus sit. Exaggeretur hic audacia & contemtus edicti regii: d. Exemplis aliorum nobilium, quibus capitale fuerit. Ergo & huic, licet principi. Leges enim personas non respiciunt.
units.tr: c. The judgement already passed on Bouteville himself, who was long ago outlawed for duels. Here his audacity and contempt for the royal Edict are to be stressed. d. The examples of other nobles, for whom it was a capital matter. Therefore it should be so for him too, although he is a prince, for the laws do not regard persons.

units.la: Concluf. Ergo fiat justitia ex Lege : Addatur wáꝉ& magno exemplo, magna ac adulta vitia compescenda esse.
units.tr: Conclusion. Therefore let justice be done according to the law. Add [illegible]: that great and grown vices must be restrained by a great example.

units.la: Defensio Butevillii in statu Qualit. absoluto & assumpto.
units.tr: Defence of Bouteville in the absolute and assumed state.

units.la: A. Exord. Oblique taxet formam judicii ex privilegio personæ;
units.tr: A. Exordium. He obliquely criticises the form of the trial on the ground of the privilege of his person;

units.la: I. Quod persona talis sit, quæ non coram Parlamento, sed coram ducibus & paribus conveniri jure queat.
units.tr: I. That his is a person who by right may be summoned not before Parliament but before the dukes and peers.

units.la: II. Quod tamen privilegium fori allegare nolit adversus Augustum hunc confessum, & adversus voluntatem regis : in cujus gratia amplissimum speret præsidium.
units.tr: II. That nevertheless he is unwilling to plead the privilege of the court against this august assembly and against the will of the king, in whose favour he hopes for the very ample protection.

units.la: B. Propof. Se non negare factum, nec justitiam ejus allegaturum; sed objecta tantum breviter excusaturum, ad gratiam regis supplicThey provocaturum.
units.tr: B. Proposition. That he does not deny the deed, nor will he plead its justice; but that he will only briefly excuse the charges and appeal to the king's grace.

units.la: C. Examen objectorum in statu absoluto
units.tr: C. Examination of the objections in the absolute state.

units.la: I. Ex ratione facti;
units.tr: I. From the nature of the deed;

units.la: ad a. & b. Fatetur & deplorat exitium, at obstinationem animi & contemptum legum negat; dicitque insolentia adversarii, qui ipsum aliquoties provocarit, se audacius egisse impatiens injuriæ. Hic jactet antiquam ac illustrem prosapiam, quæ tot Conestablios numeret, cui indignum sit ferre injurias Marchionis novitii.
units.tr: As to a. and b. He confesses and laments the death, but denies a stubborn spirit and contempt of the laws; and he says that, being unable to bear injury, he acted more boldly because of the insolence of his opponent, who had challenged him several times. Here he boasts of his ancient and illustrious lineage, which counts so many Constables, and to which it is unworthy to bear the injuries of a newly made Marquis.

units.la: ad c. Non posse trahi in consequentiam 1. cum raro tali personæ tam justa causa sit. 2. cum gratiæ omnia deputaturus sit, non justitiæ.
units.tr: As to c. It cannot be drawn into a consequence (1) because for such a person there is rarely so just a cause; (2) because he will attribute everything to grace, not to justice.

units.la: II. Ex testimoniis.
units.tr: II. From the testimonies.

units.la: ad a. Distinguendo inter homicidia & duella, illa LL. damnata, hæc non illico, & si maxime, contraria tamen consuetudine inter illustres approbata est: Ipsum regem Franciscum I. Carolo V. Imp. obtulisse duellum. Si quid labis hic sit, indulgendum esse consuetudini. Patrem regis Henricum IV. connivisse duellatoribus. &c.
units.tr: As to a. By distinguishing between homicides and duels: the laws condemn the former, but not at once the latter; and even if it is against the law, it has nevertheless been approved among the illustrious by a contrary custom. King Francis I himself offered a duel to Charles V the Emperor. If there is any stain here, it must be indulged to custom. King Henry IV's father connived at duellists, etc.

units.la: ad b. Edictum moderari duella, non excludere allegationem justæ causæ, qualis hic sit.
units.tr: As to b. The Edict moderates duels; it does not exclude the plea of a just cause, such as this one is.

units.la: ad c. & d. Si aliis capitale fuerit & sibi luctuosum, regiæ clementiæ esse mitigare poenam ex consideratione meritorum familiæ Mommorantiorum.
units.tr: As to c. and d. If the penalty is capital for others and grievous for him, it is for the royal clemency to mitigate the punishment in consideration of the merits of the Montmorency family.

units.la: D. Refugium ad gratiam regis in statu assumpto.
units.tr: D. Recourse to the king's grace in the assumed state.

units.la: I. Mitigat delictum.
units.tr: I. He mitigates the offence.

units.la: a. Quia à provocato & lacessito commissum ex cupiditate gloriæ.
units.tr: a. Because it was committed by the one provoked and challenged, out of a desire for glory.

units.la: b. Quia vulneratus tantum sit adversarius, & spes sit ipsum sanatum iri. Quia sua jactantia malum hoc sibi accesserit.
units.tr: b. Because his opponent was only wounded and there is hope he will be healed. Because this evil came upon him through his own boasting.

units.la: II. Deprecatur rationibus petitis
units.tr: II. He pleads on grounds drawn

units.la: a. A qualitate personæ, quæ sit 1. ex familia Mommorantiorum illustrissima & optime merita. 2. Spes unica familiæ. 3. apta ad servitia bellica pro salute regni.
units.tr: a. From the quality of his person, who is (1) of the most illustrious Montmorency family and of very great service; (2) the family's only hope; (3) fit for military service for the safety of the kingdom.

units.la: b. Ab insita clementia regis, qui in opprobrium tot familiarum illustrium, quibus sanguine junctus sit, nolit exemplum rigoris statuere in sanguine Mommorant.
units.tr: b. From the innate clemency of the king, who, to the disgrace of so many illustrious families to which he is related by blood, will not wish to make an example of severity in the blood of Montmorency.

units.la: E. Concluf. Petens gratiosam condonationem, quam & tot una Principes petant, & exspectent.
units.tr: E. Conclusion. He seeks a gracious pardon, which so many princes also seek and hope for.

units.la: Decretum fuit in Parlam. ut juxta leges publicè in foro Parienfi una cum socio, Capello decolletur; nisi rex gratiam faciat; quæ negata à rege, executio facta est juxta sententiam Parlamenti.
units.tr: It was decreed in Parliament that, according to the laws, he be publicly beheaded in the Paris square together with his companion Capel, unless the king grant grace; this grace being refused by the king, the execution was carried out in accordance with the sentence of Parliament.
